summary: Temporary decrypted inference payload query access for privacy QA and redaction verification
requested_access_scope: One-time, read-only, decrypted search queries against a bounded set of 1,200 production inference sessions identified by hashed_request_id. Access must be scoped to field-limited payloads (prompt, model_id, timestamp, response_tokens) and exclude any customer PII fields flagged by the redaction classifier. Data will be delivered as a pseudonymized CSV over an encrypted S3 presigned URL with KMS envelope encryption.
data_minimization_plan: Apply automated field-sieve to drop any fields matching PI patterns (emails, credit-card-like digits, SSN patterns). Apply deterministic pseudonymization to identifiers (sha256 with salt stored in Secrets Manager). Run the existing redaction classifier and remove any tokens marked HIGH_RISK. Only include model inference context up to 2k tokens per session to limit exposure.
retention_and_disposition: Export artifact will be available for a maximum of 72 hours from creation. After approval window closes, S3 object will be moved to a locked bucket and then securely deleted using a 3-step purge (object delete, version purge, and KMS rewrap revoke) within 7 days. Access logs and approval trail retained per compliance baseline.
description:
Issue summary:
Requesting timeboxed access to query and export a highly-scoped set of production inference payloads to validate the new automated redaction rules against known customer reports.

Impact:
This is for an internal privacy QA exercise. Potential exposure risk is limited by strong minimization rules but the data originates from production inference traffic. No new writes or replays to production are required.

Background:
Customer Support reported several examples where automated redaction missed structured tokens in streaming outputs. Privacy engineering and product want to run targeted validations against live historically-seen sessions to verify fixes across models and tokenization variants.

Request details:
- Number of sessions: ~1,200 hashed_request_ids (list provided in linked confluence).
- Fields: prompt, response_tokens (truncated to 2k tokens), model_id, timestamp, breadcrumb metadata (region, route).
- Access method: read-only presigned S3 export with KMS envelope. No direct DB or console access.
- Duration: export created within 24h of approval, downloadable for 72h.

Security controls and justifications:
- Two-person control: export must be initiated by SRE and pulled by Privacy engineer; both people logged in IDP and referenced in approval block.
- KMS-protected envelope, CMK access restricted to requestor and SRE execution role.
- Deterministic pseudonymization of identifiers to prevent re-identification while enabling join analysis.

Required actions before export:
1) Privacy review sign-off (confirm minimization and classifier thresholds).
2) SRE to create export job with IAM role scoping and generate presigned URL.
3) Security to verify KMS key policy and two-person control.
4) Product to confirm scope list of hashed_request_ids.

Post-export requirements:
- Submit a short QA summary and redaction delta metrics to the privacy runbook.
- Confirm deletion steps completed and provide deletion proof (S3 delete markers + audit log).

Notes:
- If any HIGH_RISK tokens are found during QA, stop and notify Security and Legal immediately; do not escalate data further.
- This task aims to reduce false-negatives in automated redaction across the serving runtime, with measurable KPIs (reduction in missed tokens by >80% on sample).
